hook: Your agent says it's done. How do you know it works?
idea: T S laws lets you write the rules, in TypeScript. The agent writes the code. And nothing lands until your rules hold.
run: Here are five laws, running against code an agent wrote.
catch: One fails. The sort quietly drops duplicates. And you get the smallest input that breaks it, with a seed to replay it.
source: A law is a few lines of plain TypeScript. The compiler understands it.
proved: Some laws are not just tested. They are proved, for every number there is.
lock: And the agent cannot water them down. Only you can accept a law.
browser: It runs in a real browser too. Components, accessibility, speed. All live.
e2e: Even a whole app, server and all.
outro: T S laws. Trust the code you did not write.
